This diversity allows students to explore different areas of interest and benefit from a rich and varied educational experience. The university also stands out for its international partnerships and collaborations with prestigious institutions worldwide. These alliances provide students and researchers with opportunities to engage in collaborative projects and exchange ideas with experts from diverse backgrounds.
Furthermore, the University of Toulouse is deeply committed to innovative research. It hosts numerous renowned research laboratories where researchers work on innovative projects in a multitude of fields, from medicine to aerospace to social sciences. The ANITI institute, dedicated to artificial intelligence, is one of the most important project coordinated by the University of Toulouse. EnduroSat S.a.r.l (Luxembourg) was established as a specialized branch of EnduroSat Group to serve the Luxembourgish market and international clients by providing high expertise of mission management. It aims to develop and commercialize a streamlined mission management service for the future markets of earth observation (EO) and satellite communication (SatCom) as well as for satellite constellations in very low and low earth orbits (LEO/VLEO). 
EnduroSat S.a.r.l. services include project management for a satellite platform development, integration and testing, mission design and mission management, and operation of high-performance satellites and customized satellite missions. As part of the EnduroSat Group, Endurosat S.a.r.l. benefits from considerable flight heritage as currently there are more than 500 systems flying in orbit. The satellite platforms, which are developed by EnduroSat Group are software-defined and in-flight configurable – the parameters of the satellite can be updated in orbit according to the customer’s needs. The unique features of EnduroSat’s platforms include:
• Plug & play on hardware and software level
• In-orbit configurability and update capability
• Multiple hardware and software redundancies
EnduroSat S.a.r.l, as a newly established branch, leverages the existing expertise of the EnduroSat Group which has built a solid experience by providing solutions for many successful projects. entityDescription: ADAPTA Studio is a spinoff of Politecnico di Milano that has made 3D accessible to everyone through the development of algorithms for the optimization and management of models, spaces, and scans, patented and usable through a Cloud service. ADAPTA has designed a cloud service, "AMAZ3D," to democratize the use and distribution of 3D models, spaces, and scans (hereinafter referred to as 3D assets) to meet the growing demand for digital content. In fact, one of the main challenges in the field of 3D applications (Gaming, CAD, Digital Twin, Training, etc.) today is to have real-time interactions with the highest possible graphical performance. ADAPTA has developed innovative algorithms that significantly reduce the polygon count and weight of 3D assets while maintaining the quality and final graphical performance as much as possible, making it usable on any type of device (PC, smartphone, tablet, headsets, etc.) with a focus on digital multichannel for the end user (Web, Mobile, Augmented and Virtual Reality) with optimal performance. Furthermore, AMAZ3D not only optimizes the 3D model but also manages the entire document flow (storage, versioning, sharing, etc.) through a repository and a 3D viewer integrable into apps and third-party systems. The company is currently evolving AMAZ3D to also support next-generation 3D tools for the automatic reconstruction of three-dimensional assets based on artificial intelligence techniques such as NERF/Gaussian Splatting.

Pileus Scandinavia, further in the text called Pileus, is a newly started company that aims to bring new technology from Luleå University of Technology, regarding ice detection and forecast for ice formation on wind turbines, to the market.
The technology has been validated during two winter seasons together with Vattenfall and Statkraft and has proven to be superior to other technology available today. Pileus technology is able to detect 97% of cases, which can be compared to today's system that can handle 2%.
Being able to detect with very high accuracy and accuracy when ice begins to accumulate on wind turbines and being able to provide a forecast of what the risk looks like for the next 24 hours provides very great benefits for wind power producers. The advantages concern both electricity production, security and pricing linked to the common electricity market, Nord Pool. Energy losses due to ice and snow can amount to 10-15% of total production during a winter, i.e. large energy loss and reduced revenues for owners of wind farms.
By using Pileus technology, this figure can be greatly reduced and electricity production optimized by using our forecast for weather and icing.

In AID, we take our passion and commitment beyond borders, positively impacting communities around the world. Proud of our global influence, we do not confine ourselves to regions where we have already worked. At AID, we are dedicated to forging strategic partnerships that allow us to work in harmony with the needs and goals of these prominent institutions, ensuring that our architecture is not only aesthetic and functional but also a catalyst for development and global well-being. These partnerships reflect our shared commitment to generating a positive and enduring impact on society.
We promote the general interests of society through architecture and engineering, disciplines aimed at satisfying the basic needs of human beings, such as housing in dignified and secure conditions. We recognize the fundamental implications of our activities on collective well-being, including proper land management, responsible management of natural resources, and the preservation of our heritage. To achieve this, we commit to transitioning towards areas of cooperation and other ethical sectors that concretely and significantly improve people's quality of life. We focus on collaborating with clients who share our commitment and are dedicated to supporting sectors, areas, and populations that align with the values and objectives of AID.

entityDescription:
With the advent of large launchers, the price of cargo to low Earth orbit has plummeted to new lows. Soon, a future in which cargo prices from here to LEO are the same as from here to Shenzhen seems possible. This opens up the prospect of using space as a place for economic activity, not just for data, telecommunications or images, but also for physical goods and materials. Space is indeed a very attractive place to do this: the absence of gravity opens up drastically simpler synthesis routes for a range of chemical, physical and biological compounds, while the environment provides infinite free energy, heat, cold and quasi-perfect vacuum - commodities that would require drastic amounts of energy on Earth.
As attractive as this vision is, the current state of technology stands in the way of this future. In fact, with the exception of the launcher, the entire space technology stack in use today is still based on paradigms from over half a century ago, when space assets were essentially very expensive disposable items. As travel to and from space has become routine, this needs to change to make the entire industry sustainable and resource efficient.
Starflight Dynamics' mission is to provide the enabling technologies to bring industry to space and enable future production there. As such, the company is working to provide the full range of services required, from reusable transport platforms to reusable space cargo containers and, of course, large solar-powered production platforms that will be the production sites of the future. 
Starflight Dynamics will generate revenue from two main sources:
- Once established, the company will build and operate robotic in-orbit production facilities, where customers can run their processes in dedicated production cargo containers.
- Along the way, the company will commercialise the technologies developed for this, from agile and long-endurance platforms to re-entry technologies and the like. To this end, the company has partnered with established industrialists in the field to provide derived products for niche applications.

entityName: Instytut Geofizyki Polskiej Akademii Nauk (Institute of Geophysics of the Polish Academy of Sciences)
entityDescription:
Institute of Geophysics of the Polish Academy of Sciences - a scientific institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences based in Warsaw, dealing with research and monitoring of geophysical processes. He is a member of the Center for Earth and Planet Research - GeoPlanet. Since 2023, the director of the Institute is prof. Ph.D. Paweł M. Rowiński.
The Institute of Geophysics has been operating since 1953, initially (until 1970) as the Department of Geophysics. In the initial period, research conducted there was limited to selected issues in the field of seismology, physics of the Earth's interior and terrestrial magnetism; other fields of geophysics were gradually added: physics of the atmosphere, ionosphere and magnetosphere, oceanology, planetary geodesy, hydrology.
In the years 1973-1978, some departments separated from the Institute of Geophysics of the Polish Academy of Sciences, creating independent research institutions: the Institute of Oceanology of the Polish Academy of Sciences and the Space Research Center of the Polish Academy of Sciences.
The Institute is currently conducting research in the following areas:
• Seismology - analysis of earthquakes and tremors induced by mining activities, seismicity of the European Union area and more broadly,
• Seismic studies of the lithosphere - the structure and geodynamics of the Earth's crust and upper mantle obtained based on deep seismic soundings and natural seismicity. organization and interpretation of active and passive seismic experiments aimed at identifying the structure of the crust and upper mantle of the Earth,
• Geophysical imaging - development and application of innovative imaging techniques, especially those based on the full wave field, seismic processing, depth imaging and denoising of seismic data.
• Theoretical geophysics – analysis of the physical laws governing geophysical processes and development of mathematical and numerical methods for describing these phenomena,
• Magnetism - development of magnetotelluric research methods, numerical modeling of electromagnetic induction processes in the Earth's interior, regional research on the structure of the Earth's crust, paleomagnetic research and magnetic properties of intrusive and sedimentary rocks,
• Polar and marine research - analysis of geophysical and environmental data obtained at the Polish Polar Station on Spitsbergen and Hornsund, research on changes in abiotic features of the natural environment in the polar zones,
• Hydrology and hydrodynamics – transport and mixing of pollutants in surface waters, modeling of flood wave transformation using hydraulic and hydrological models, modeling of flood risk by implementing the latest achievements of the statistical theory of extreme phenomena, climate change,
• Atmospheric physics - analysis of the variability of the ozone layer and solar radiation on various time scales, transparency of the atmosphere, atmospheric electricity, structure of storm clouds and discharges.
Currently, the Institute conduct 86 projects of scientific.

PLP Architecture is a London-based studio of architects, designers and researchers who value the transformative role of ideas and the capacity for architecture to inspire. The practice has produced some of the world’s greenest, most intelligent, and ground-breaking designs through a profound commitment to social, economic, and environmental values.

Led by an experienced and dedicated group of partners who have worked together for more than three decades, we draw from a rich history and experience working together across a diverse portfolio of more than 500 projects around the world. We value innovation and creativity and strive to test conventional limits, producing intelligent, ground-breaking, and exciting designs. We work across typologies and beyond the traditional boundaries of architecture, interiors and master planning services, providing branding and positioning research, engagement strategies, and graphic, interior, product, and furniture design. 

The foundation of our work lies in a commitment to a high quality of urban life, excellence in the handling of material, space and light, and an optimism about architecture’s potential to enrich our society. We approach every project brief with an open mind and develop an architectural response that addresses the unique challenges presented by our clients’ goals and specific site, crafting an architecture that responds to each location’s climate, history, and culture. We embrace collaboration, and our design process extracts and harness the knowledge and experience of our clients and consultants. 

Research also plays an important part in our work, and we consistently strived to push boundaries and redefine limits. PLP Labs serves as our in-house think tank to explore topics as varied as cultural engagement, brief writing and storytelling, and district-wide activation strategies.
